youtube.title: Vikings Never Wore Horned Helmets. An Opera Did
youtube.description:
Archaeologists have never found a horned Viking helmet. The only nearly complete Viking helmet ever found, from Gjermundbu in Norway (discovered 1943), is a rounded iron cap with an eye-and-nose guard and no horns. The horns came from costume designer Carl Emil Doepler's designs for the 1876 premiere of Wagner's Ring cycle at Bayreuth. Horned helmets did exist in Scandinavia: the bronze Veksø helmets from Denmark, which a 2022 study dated to around 900 BC, more than 1,500 years before the Viking Age.

📂 Case File #060: Viking Helmets
